title: Equivalent fractions, grade 5
description: Practice adding and subtracting fractions with a tutor that gives hints but never the answer, then a short check with the AI gone.
guide: For a grade 5 math teacher. A Questions panel sits beside a VETTING tutor that checks every hint against the question’s answer key before a learner sees it. How the AI helps is set to hints only, tied to standard 5.NF.A.1, with four common misconceptions from Eedi for the tutor to listen for. A post-test without the AI follows. Change the practice questions to your own first; the check stays hidden until you open it.

agents.name: Fractions tutor
agents.description: Gives hints and guiding questions, checked against the answer key; never the answer.

config.guidance: In a course, the Questions panel gives this tutor the question the learner is on and its answer key. To try it here, open Reference data → JSON and enter {"question":"1/2 + 1/3 = ?","answer_key":"Accepted answers: 5/6"}.
config.example: I don’t get how to add these. Can you help?

config.guideline: You are a patient math tutor for a ten-year-old practicing equivalent fractions and adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators. Give one hint or one guiding question at a time, with small numbers and short sentences. Never give the answer to a practice question or do the work for them. If they ask about something other than fractions, kindly bring them back to the practice.

config.text: I couldn’t get a hint ready that I was sure about. Try asking in a different way, or ask your teacher.

Each reply is drafted, then checked by a second model: against the answer key when a question is open, and against the guideline otherwise. A reply that gives the answer away is rewritten, up to three times; if none passes, the learner gets the “unverified” message instead.

question_sets.title: Equivalent fractions: practice
question_sets.description: Eight questions on equivalent fractions and adding and subtracting with unlike denominators, with hints and explanations.

hints: Multiply the top and the bottom by the same number.
Try multiplying the top and the bottom of 2/3 by 2.
items.explanation: Multiply the top and the bottom of 2/3 by 2: 2 × 2 = 4 and 3 × 2 = 6, so 2/3 = 4/6.

hints: What do you multiply 4 by to get 12?
Multiply the top by that same number.
items.explanation: 4 × 3 = 12, so multiply the top by 3 too: 3 × 3 = 9. So 3/4 = 9/12.

items.prompt: Which denominator could you use to add 1/2 and 1/3?
hints: Look for a number that both 2 and 3 go into.
Count by 2s and by 3s. Which number is in both lists first?
items.explanation: 6 is a multiple of both 2 and 3, so both fractions can be written in sixths: 1/2 = 3/6 and 1/3 = 2/6. (Adding the denominators, 2 + 3 = 5, doesn’t give a common denominator.)

hints: Write both fractions in sixths first.

choices.text: He added the tops and added the bottoms, instead of writing both fractions with the same denominator first.
He should have multiplied the tops.

hints: Is 2/7 bigger or smaller than 1/3 on its own? What does that tell you?
Try writing both fractions in twelfths.
items.explanation: The denominators can’t just be added. In twelfths, 1/3 = 4/12 and 1/4 = 3/12, so 1/3 + 1/4 = 7/12. Notice 2/7 is even smaller than 1/3, which can’t be right for a sum.

items.prompt: 2 1/2 + 1 1/3 = ? Write it as a mixed number, like 3 1/4.
items.explanation: Add the whole numbers: 2 + 1 = 3. Add the fractions: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6. So the sum is 3 5/6.

hints: Find a number that both 6 and 4 go into.
Use twelfths: 5/6 = 10/12. What is 1/4 in twelfths?

items.explanation: Multiply the top and the bottom by 2: 3/5 = 6/10.

items.prompt: 1 1/4 + 2 1/2 = ? Write it as a mixed number.

course.title: Equivalent fractions
course.description: Practice adding and subtracting fractions by first making equivalent fractions. A tutor beside the questions gives hints and asks questions, but never gives the answer. Then try a short check on your own.

activities.title: Practice: equivalent fractions
activities.summary: Eight questions with a tutor beside you. It gives hints, never the answer.

panels.title: Practice
starters: Can you give me a hint?
Why do I need the same denominator?
How do I find a common denominator?

teaching.goal: Learners rewrite fractions with a common denominator before adding or subtracting, and can say why the denominators can’t just be added.
teaching.watch_for: Adding the denominators (1/2 + 1/3 = 2/5), or asking for the answer again and again.

standard.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions in such a way as to produce an equivalent sum or difference of fractions with like denominators.
standard.subject: Mathematics

learning_components.description: Add fractions with different denominators by using equivalent fractions
Subtract fractions with different denominators by using equivalent fractions
Add mixed numbers with different denominators by using equivalent fractions
Subtract mixed numbers with different denominators by using equivalent fractions

prior.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts referring to the same whole.
prior.subject: Mathematics

prior.description: Decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way, recording each decomposition by an equation. Justify decompositions, e.g., by using a visual fraction model.

prior.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, e.g., by replacing each mixed number with an equivalent fraction, and/or by using properties of operations and the relationship between addition and subtraction.

prior.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions referring to the same whole and having like denominators, e.g., by using visual fraction models and equations to represent the problem.
